name: Dale Malik
life: “I still remember my last night aboard with a coat too stiff to fold.” People around the downtown fountain know Dale by a small Thursday habit. Dale keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I kept the salt from my last deck shift in my cuff. I wish I'd said something before the rinse.
appearance: Dale has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. In conversation Dale gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: Dale finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To take the last deck salt home intact.
family: Julia Cao is Dale’s stepsibling. Dale calls about good news first. Julia is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *A four o'clock kitchen*, Julia says, “I want the port to subsidize a workers' meal without owning the menu or the cook's schedule.”
connections: Teresa Ellis. They establish which salt coat belongs to which member of the deck crew.

reactions.situation: A coat's owner claims the crystals in the lining
reactions.response: Dale sets the coat aside until the owner can identify the crystals privately.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Dale puts distance between the frightened person and the argument and asks nearby staff for help.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Dale waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
